questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The breadth of academic opportunities. I knew UoE would have a plethora of interesting English Lit courses and I was not dissapointed!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When prioritising courses, choose something you maybe wouldn't otherwise have tried! At UoE you do three courses (at least in my case) and getting to immerse yourself in something novel is so worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information itself was accesible, the amount is just, unsurprisingly, overwhelming. Prepare and familiarise yourself with the different platforms and you'll be fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Visiting Students Office at UoE helped me with some of the initial processes

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult, but that was due to my own misunderstanding of the system/pricing. I ended up on the waitlist for accomodation, but got an offer a week later.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Edinburgh, public transport is fortunately so easy, so getting to uni is no issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a repetitive process, so make sure to check and recheck whether you've done the proper paperwork!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The UoE course registration process was confusing at first, as the availability of courses on the registration page did not reflect the actual availibility. I got in contact with the Study Abroad office and was luckily assured of the availibility. There is plenty of detailed information on the courses themselves which helped a lot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Study Abroad office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got two of my top five courses. The third was not a priority of mine, but I ended up loving it!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try something you wouldn't have at your home institution!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was wonderfully clear how much the department cared about the programmes, the students and the atmosphere.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to the difference in BA programme lenghts in Denmark and the UK, I was only able to take 3rd year courses. Because of this, the expectatons in the 3rd year courses felt more like 2nd year courses to me personally.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall, the same level of congeniality and openness as I have come to appreciate at UCPH were present at UoE. The professors were invested in the students opinions and in many instances, the seminar's direction were led by the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Early Modern Comedy, Shakespeare: Modes and Genres, and The Making of Modern Fantasy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above! The Shakespeare course demands a bit of prior interest, of course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not many unexpected costs, personally. The travel insurance, but I fixed that before leaving. It is worth to prepare yourself for the cost of food and grocery items.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I personally couldn't take advantage of this, but many of my friends got the Young Scots card (available for under 21s) which gave them mostly free public transport!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Too many to count. The UoE societies are truly astounding, and of these many are completely free!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Dancing classes, walking groups, book societies!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands! ESN does guided weekend trips all over the highlands, really worth it. Bus-travel (FlixBus etc) is the best travel method in my opinion, both due to cost and scenery on the way.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Incredibly easy. The scottish people are so wonderfully welcoming and I never felt alone or unwanted.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to welcome events, make plans, go on trips together, study together, sign up for non-academic classes together!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Literally only understanding the Glaswegian accent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness. The amount of celtic and gaelic cultural remnants and traditions still upheld by the locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Explore the city as much as you can
Visit the highlands and hike if possible
Make friends with both locals and other exchange students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pack less than you think you will need, really only the necessities. In my case, I acquired 45 books for a criminally low price and making room for that in my luggage will be interesting.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my new group of friends from all over the world. I know that this group will last beyond this exchange and I am eternally grateful.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making time for all the stuff I wanted to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Prepare yourself for different kinds of examination/essay writing expectation (at least in the case of English lit). For instance, at UoE, being able to present close-readings of several texts within a narrow wordcount is the key, rather than a single (or comparative) close-reading.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
